title: India's Cabinet just approved its last two semiconductor plants - and the program is now complete
sources: PM India (official press release) - Cabinet approves two more semiconductor manufacturing units with cumulative investment of more than Rs 3,900 crore
The Tribune - Cabinet approves two more semiconductor manufacturing units in Gujarat with cumulative investment of over Rs 3,900 crore
caption:
India's Cabinet just approved its last two semiconductor plants. That completes a 12-project program worth Rs 1.64 lakh crore.

The Union Cabinet approved two new semiconductor units in Gujarat - Crystal Matrix in Dholera (GaN-based display modules) and Suchi Semicon in Surat (discrete chip packaging, 1,033+ million chips/year capacity) - with combined investment of about Rs 3,900 crore. This completes the India Semiconductor Mission's first phase: 12 approved projects spanning Gujarat, Assam, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha.

Phase one of a semiconductor mission usually means one or two flagship plants. India's phase one means twelve, spread across five states.

Sources: PM India, The Tribune (2026)
